questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to translate security requirements into policy-as-code, enforce across workload types, and validate in CI. It also probes tool choice (Kyverno vs OPA Gatekeeper), namespace scoping, and test design.

## Key Concepts
- Runtime security posture with securityContext fields
- Policy engines: Kyverno, OPA Gatekeeper
- Resource types: Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets
- Local and CI validation strategies

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno cluster policy example
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-runtime-hardening
spec:
  rules:
  - name: require-secure-pod
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ['Deployment','StatefulSet','DaemonSet']
    validate:
      message: 'Containers must be non-root, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and drop ALL capabilities'
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - name: '*'
                securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  runAsUser: 1000
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
                  capabilities:
                    drop: ['ALL']
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest example (violates rules)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: fail-noncompliant
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: fail
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/app:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsUser: 0
          privileged: true
          capabilities:
            add: ['NET_ADMIN']
      volumes:
      - name: data
        hostPath:
          path: /data
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest example
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: compliant
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/app:1.2.3
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ['ALL']
```

- Verification steps: locally run kyverno test, simulate with kubectl apply and audit via kyverno CLI; CI gate runs kyverno/opa checks on PR.

- How would you handle exceptions per-namespace or per-tenant?
- How would you measure false positives in CI across multiple clusters?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design end-to-end controls around data contracts, provenance, and policy enforcement in a multi-tenant data platform. Candidates must describe concrete artifacts, tools, and integration points, not abstractions.

## Key Concepts
- Data contracts and central registry validation
- Software bill of materials (SBOM) generation
- Reproducible build digest tying code, contract, and dependencies
- Artifact signing and attestations
- Policy-as-code (Kyverno/OPA) for admission control

## Code Example
```yaml
# .github/workflows/contract-ci.yml
name: Contract CI
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Validate contract
        run: |
          npm ci && npm run validate-contract -- --registry https://registry.example.com
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          npm ci && npm run generate-sbom
      - name: Compute digest
        run: |
          echo -n "$(git rev-parse --verify HEAD)" > digest.txt
          shasum -a 256 contract.json sbom.json >> digest.txt
      - name: Attest
        run: |
          echo "attestation" && cat digest.txt
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you roll out this gate to multiple cloud regions with differing registry endpoints?
- How would you test failure modes (invalid contract, missing SBOM, digest mismatch) in CI and in runtime?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design runtime, policy-driven security for multi-tenant clusters, including per-tenant exceptions, scalable policy storage, and practical CI validation.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Rego enforcement
- Runtime security: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, hostPath, privileged, SETUID checks
- Central PolicyStore for per-tenant overrides
- CI validation: dry-run, Gatekeeper evaluation, and manifest validation

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: runtimepolicy
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: RuntimePolicy
        listKind: RuntimePolicyList
        plural: runtimepolicies
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package runtimepolicy
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      {
        input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.runAsNonRoot != true
        msg := "container must run as non-root"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      {
        any_cont := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
        not any_cont.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem
        msg := "container must have readOnlyRootFilesystem: true"
      }
      # Additional rules for hostPath, privileged, and SETUID would follow similarly
```

```yaml
# Constraint (example)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: RuntimePolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-runtime-policy
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: ["apps"]
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    namespaces: ["tenant-a-*"]
```

- How would you measure policy evaluation latency at scale?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to enforce secure secret handling across multi-cloud clusters, using policy-as-code, and integrating cert-manager with GitOps pipelines.

## Key Concepts
- Policy as code (Kyverno/OPA)
- cert-manager Certificate -> Secret flow
- ExternalSecret / SecretStore integration
- CI gating and canary verification

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno policy (example)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-inline-tls-and-enforce-secretref
spec:
  validationFailureAction: fail
  rules:
  - name: deny-inline-tls
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "TLS data must come from cert-manager SecretRef; do not inline certificates"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              volumes:
              - secret:
                  secretName: "?!*"
```

```rego
# OPA/ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (illustrative)
package kubernetes.admission

deny[{"msg":"inline certs not allowed"}] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Deployment" or input.request.kind.kind == "StatefulSet"
  some i
  secret := input.request.object.spec.template.spec.volumes[i]
  secret.secretName != "" # ensure SecretRef used, not inline data
}
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (inline cert example)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tls-secret
type: kubernetes.io/tls
data:
  tls.crt: LS0tLS1CRUdJTiBDRVJUSUZJQ0FURS0tLS0t... # inline cert data
  tls.key: LS0tLS1CRUdJTiBSU0EgUFJ...
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (SecretRef to cert-manager Secret)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      volumes:
      - name: tls
        secret:
          secretName: my-cert-manager-secret
```

```yaml
# CI validation steps (high level)
- lint manifests
- run policy gate (Kyverno/OPA) on PR
- validate that Deployment references cert-manager Secret (no inline data)
- run a quick canary test in a staging cluster
```

- How would you test this in a mono-repo with many teams?

## Why This Is Asked

- SBOM generation and ingest (CycloneDX)

- Namespace labeling and non-root container policies
- CI integration and runtime verification

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8simage signing
spec:
  crd: {}
  targets:
  - [' admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh','' ]
  rego: |
    package gatekeeper.image_signing
    violation["Image is not signed"] {
      input.review.kind.kind == "Deployment"
      not input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers[_].image | image_signing.sign
    }
```
